subject.title: Feature: enrich usage/status JSON with agent, cron, and channel labels

question: Should OpenClaw promote agent/cron/channel attribution to a stable public usage/status JSON contract, and which privacy-safe fields should be included?
rationale: The request crosses status JSON, gateway usage APIs, session metadata, cron metadata, and channel privacy, so maintainers need to choose the public contract before implementation.

options.title: Define a narrow stable attribution contract
options.body: Add optional non-sensitive fields such as agentId, sessionKind, cronJobId/name, channel, model, and runtime to the usage/status JSON rows while keeping target ids omitted by default.

options.title: Keep the surface internal for now
options.body: Leave dashboards to join sessions, cron, and channel metadata until maintainers are ready to own a stable export schema.

options.title: Track only CLI/TUI label display separately
options.body: Handle human-readable cron labels in the narrower status-display issue and defer machine-readable usage attribution.

recommendation.title: Define a narrow stable attribution contract
recommendation.body: Add optional non-sensitive fields such as agentId, sessionKind, cronJobId/name, channel, model, and runtime to the usage/status JSON rows while keeping target ids omitted by default.

likelyOwner.reason: This is a product-contract decision across existing status, usage, and privacy surfaces where recent shared usage/status history points to steipete for routing.
